t: we fine him the weight of fifty sela of refined silver. They penalize him to pay fifty sela of pure silver. The sela is a coin weighing three hundred eighty-four barleycorns (Hilchot Shekalim 1:2).
any woman violated in the field... and any woman violated in the city. The distinction between field and city is based on what is stated in Deuteronomy 22:23-27.
she is presumed to have been forced. We assume she was forced, and she does not need to prove this.
because she did not cry out. For had she cried out in the city, her voice would have been heard.
unless witnesses testify that she was forced etc.. For in such a case it will be clear that although she did not cry out, she was certainly forced.
or that her father did not want. For the daughter is in his domain until she comes of age, and he receives the money of her betrothal (Hilchot Ishut 3:11).
that he did not want to marry. That the seducer himself does not want to marry her.
rather he writes her a ketubah like other virgins. Whose ketubah is two hundred dinars (ibid. 10:7), and he may divorce her if he wishes (compare below halakhah 4).
lame. She has a defect in her leg that causes her to limp.
blind. Unable to see.
so that it not be easy in his eyes to send her away. As explained in Hilchot Ishut 10:7.
even among those liable by a positive commandment. She is forbidden to him by a positive commandment (Hilchot Ishut 1:8).
a second-degree prohibited relation. One forbidden to him by rabbinic law (ibid. halakhah 6).
an indecent matter was found in her after he married her. An act of adultery that forbids her to her husband (see Hilchot Gerushin 11:14).
for he is commanded to marry a virgin. See Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 17:13.

a negative commandment that was converted into a positive one. A negative commandment for which there is an explicit command to rectify the transgression by a specific act, thereby shifting it to a positive commandment, for which one is not flogged.
unless he did not fulfill the positive commandment attached to it. For if he has no possibility of fulfilling the positive commandment, he is flogged.
as will be explained in Hilchot Sanhedrin. 16:4.
or who was betrothed to another. And he is thereby forbidden to take her back (Hilchot Gerushin 11:12).
in the normal manner. In the usual manner of intercourse, in the place of virginity.
warning. A warning before committing the transgression about the prohibition and its punishment.
and from when does the girl have a fine. From what age.
until she comes of age. Until she becomes an adult, when six months have passed since she grew two pubic hairs after age twelve (see Hilchot Ishut 2:1-2).
both one who has a father and one who has no father has a fine. Although the Torah says the fine is given to the girl's father, that is only when she is in his domain (see below 2:14-15).

and the one who refused her husband. An orphaned minor whom her family married off and who refused her husband while still a minor (see Hilchot Gerushin 11:1). She has no fine because she has the law of a married woman, even if in fact she was a virgin.
and the ailonit. A woman whose sexual development is defective (for her definition see Hilchot Ishut 2:4-6); she has no fine because she is considered an adult (see there).
and the deaf-mute and the mentally incompetent woman. Who lack the understanding to guard themselves, and they have no fine because it is possible that they had relations even earlier.
and one about whom a bad name has gone out etc.. "For she is presumed to have given herself up to this willingly" (below 2:17).
and one who was divorced from marriage and is still a young virgin. Nevertheless, she has the law of a non-virgin from the time she married (see Hilchot Ishut 11:1-2; Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 19:3).
but one divorced from betrothal... and if she was seduced she has no fine. Because the fine is hers (below 2:16), and her consent to the seducer is regarded as waiving the fine.
a convert, a captive and a freed slave. They are presumed to have had relations while they were gentiles, captives or slaves, and therefore they have the law of non-virgins (Hilchot Ishut 11:2).
and a freed slave. A gentile maidservant who was freed (see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 12:17).
and she is three years old or less, she has a fine. For even if they had relations before this age, the intercourse is not considered intercourse, and they are considered virgins.
this virgin was forbidden to the rapist or seducer. So that in his intercourse with her, the rapist or seducer committed a prohibition.
if she was among those liable to karet. A forbidden relation whose transgressor is liable to karet (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 1:1-7; Hilchot Sanhedrin 19:1).

or was among those liable by negative commandments. Whose intercourse the Torah forbade with a negative commandment and for which there is no karet, such as a mamzeret to an Israelite (see Hilchot Ishut 1:7).
if they warned him. They warned him that this intercourse is forbidden to him on account of karet or a negative commandment.
he is flogged. For the forbidden intercourse.
and he does not pay a fine. For raping or seducing.
for a person is not flogged and made to pay. A person is given only one punishment, the more severe (Hilchot Sanhedrin 16:5; for more see Hilchot Genevah 3:1-2).
since he is not liable to flogging. For there is no liability to flogging without a warning (Hilchot Sanhedrin 16:4).
by rabbinic law. By enactment of the Sages.
she was among those liable to death by court. Severe forbidden relations for which there is the death penalty (for their list see Hilchot Sanhedrin 15:10-11).

"and if there is no harm, he shall surely be punished" etc.. The beginning of the verse is: "And if men strive and hurt a pregnant woman so that her children come out." Its meaning is that if one of the combatants unintentionally struck the woman and caused her to miscarry, he pays her husband the value of the children. But if the woman died of the injury, there is no monetary penalty (as the Torah states that he pays if "there is no harm"). This is not because the striker is liable to death, for one who kills unintentionally is not put to death, but because such an act carries a death penalty, and that exempts him from payments (see Hilchot Chovel 4:5-6).
it did not distinguish in it between unintentional and intentional. For one who strikes an animal, whether unintentionally or intentionally, must pay.

likewise regarding one who strikes a human life, it did not distinguish between unintentional and intentional so as to exempt him from payments. Just as when intentional he is liable to death and does not pay, so also when unintentional he does not pay, even though he is exempt from death.
provided that she die before she stands in court. But if they sued him in court, her father has already acquired the fine (below 2:15).
the value of the enjoyment of lying only. Paid for the intercourse itself, without regard to other damages that come because of the intercourse.

to pay for shame and blemish. To pay additional payments, for the humiliation and for the blemish of having become a non-virgin (the method of calculating the payment is explained below, halakhot 4-6).
in addition to the fine. On top of the fine.
the fixed. Set.
for he pays for the pain. Payment for the suffering.
so the seducer pays three etc.. And those same payments (shame, blemish and pain) are part of the system of payments of anyone who damaged another (Hilchot Chovel 1:1-10).
the fine is the same for everyone. It can be fixed equally for all classes.
and they require assessment. The court's evaluation of how much to pay that particular girl.
that one of the scoundrels and the lowliest of the lowly humiliated. That his humiliation is greater (Hilchot Chovel 3:1).
and they assess how much money is fitting for her father. etc. They estimate how much money her father and family would have been willing to pay to avoid this shame.

blemish according to her beauty etc.. In this way they check how much the value of the non-virgin has decreased compared with the virgin (for a similar method of assessing damages to limbs, see Hilchot Chovel 1:2).
according to her youth and the build of her body and according to his years and body. For the ages and build of the rapist and the victim affect the degree of pain in the rape.
"and if her father utterly refuses to give her to him". From which we learn that only if the father refused the marriage does he pay the fine.

"he shall weigh silver according to the bride-price of virgins". The amount of the fine is set according to what was customarily paid at that time to the father of the bride for the marriage of a virgin.
and marries. He takes her as a wife against his will, if she and her father want it.
she has nothing. For she has no ketubah (above 1:4).
and also not in the normal manner. From behind.

he is liable for shame and blemish. For even in intercourse not in the normal manner there is a blemish. He is also liable for the payment for pain if he raped her, but he pays a fine only for intercourse in the normal manner (above 1:8).
for she was already blemished. By the intercourse of the first man, and she is no longer a virgin.

and this one who had relations with her in the normal manner etc.. For intercourse in the normal manner obligates a fine, and adds a blemish even to one who was already blemished by intercourse not in the normal manner, though this blemish is less than the blemish of one who had no relations at all.
we have already informed you of the girls who have no fine. Above 1:9-10.
he pays pain only. For there is no shame or blemish in those lacking understanding.

is exempt from everything. For a seduced woman has no pain (above halakhah 1), and the adult and the one who refused her husband receive payments for themselves, so if they were seduced they have waived these payments.
fine. A payment that does not depend on the value of the damage caused but constitutes a punishment (for its characteristics see Hilchot Nizkei Mamon 2:7-8).
but he pays shame and blemish. And if he raped her he also pays pain (see Kesef Mishneh), because these payments are not a fine but an obligation to pay for damage.
the oath of heset. An oath enacted by the Sages, imposed on one who denies an entire claim against him.

for if he had admitted he would pay etc.. One swears only on payments that he would be liable to pay if he admitted them, and therefore one does not swear on denial of a fine. But if by admission of his mouth he would be liable even for part of the payments, the Sages enacted to obligate him to take an oath, lest he retract and admit (see Hilchot To'en VeNitan 1:15).
not so. It is not like that.
for he admitted to part of the claim. And one who admits to part pays what he admitted and swears on the rest by Torah law.
as will be explained in its place. Hilchot To'en VeNitan 1:1.
for all the glory of youth belongs to the father. The monetary rights of a girl belong to her father (for further examples see Hilchot Ishut 3:11; Hilchot Chovel UMazik 4:14).
until she comes of age or until she marries etc.. Until she leaves her father's domain for her own.

her fine alone is for herself. But the payments for shame, pain and blemish go to her father, because she is still in his domain, as the Sages expounded from the verses (see Babylonian Talmud, Ketubot 38a).
for betrothal does not remove from the father's domain. Only marriage does.
"I hereby hire my virgin daughter to this man to have relations with her". "I have been given permission to rent out my daughter to this man to have relations with her."
therefore it says, "Do not profane your daughter to make her a harlot". For it is not within the father's authority to make her a harlot, even though her monetary rights are his.
if this man left his virgin daughter available etc.. He designated her for harlotry.
for if she becomes pregnant and gives birth, it will not be known whose son he is. If many men came to her, further stumbling in the severe forbidden relations would result.
as we have explained. Above halakhah 9.

one who brings out a bad name on a daughter of Israel etc.. One who claims that he did not find signs of virginity in his wife and that she committed adultery while betrothed to him, and it turns out that he lied (for the manner of the claim see below, halakhah 6).

and his warning is from "You shall not go about as a talebearer among your people". The prohibition for which he is flogged is included in this negative commandment, which forbids talebearing and slander (see Hilchot De'ot 7:1-2).
the weight of one hundred sela of refined silver. See above, explanation at 1:1.
concerning the young woman. From when she grew two pubic hairs after age twelve; she is called a na'arah until six months pass from that time (Hilchot Ishut 2:1-2).

the verse spoke of a na'arah written in full. Throughout the Torah the word "na'arah" appears in defective spelling, "na'ar," to include the minor; only in the passage of one who brings out a bad name does it appear once in full spelling, meaning a na'arah only. Admittedly, in our text of Scripture the word appears in full spelling in another verse in the passage: "and they shall give to the father of the na'arah" (Deuteronomy 22:19; see Kesef Mishneh).
this case is tried only in the presence of the Temple. When the Temple stands (Hilchot Sanhedrin 14:11).
and in a court of twenty-three. Which are authorized to judge capital cases (ibid. 5:3).
for if the matter was found as he said etc.. That if it becomes clear that the husband's claims are true, and she committed adultery under him, she is liable to death.
but the rapist and the seducer. In whose cases there are only monetary laws.
in Hilchot Sanhedrin. 5:8.
that the wife of one who brings out a bad name shall remain under him forever. That he may not divorce her at will.
as we have explained regarding the rapist. Above 1:7.
he is flogged for divorcing her. For he can no longer take her back and fix the negative commandment.

and why should a positive commandment not come and override a negative one. This is the law in fulfilling positive commandments, that they must be performed even when a negative prohibition stands against them (see Hilchot Milah 1:9; Hilchot Nezirut 7:15).

for it is possible that she will not want etc.. A positive commandment overrides a negative one only where it is impossible to fulfill both, and then the positive commandment prevails (Hilchot Tzitzit 3:6). But here divorce may be permitted if the woman wants to be divorced, so it is possible that both will be fulfilled, and so a positive commandment does not override a negative one.

and when I inquired into the matter etc.. I investigated the matter and discovered that she committed adultery. For the absence of virginity is not grounds for punishment but only raises suspicion (see below halakhah 12).
if the matter was found true, she is stoned. Like a betrothed girl who committed adultery (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 3:4).

and if the father brought witnesses and they refuted the witnesses that the husband brought. The father's witnesses proved that the husband's witnesses are lying, since they were with them at the time of the event in a different place (for the definition of conspiring witnesses see Hilchot Edut 18:1-2).
shall be stoned. The husband's witnesses. For conspiring witnesses receive the same punishment they sought to cause by their testimony (ibid.).

and concerning this it says, "And these are the tokens of my daughter's virginity". These are the father's words against the husband's claim "I did not find your daughter a virgin." The proof that his daughter was a virgin and the husband is lying is that he brings witnesses who refute the husband's witnesses (and see below halakhah 12).
the husband again brought other witnesses etc.. The husband's second witnesses proved that the father's witnesses were false witnesses, so the first witnesses turn out to be speaking truth.
and her father's witnesses are stoned. And they also pay the fine to the husband (Hilchot Edut 21:10).

from oral tradition. The tradition of the Sages in the interpretation of the verses. For from the plain sense of the verses it would seem that the discussion is about finding signs of virginity (see further below, halakhah 12).
he is exempt from flogging and from the fine. For the law of one who brings out a bad name applies only to a na'arah (above halakhah 2).
she is stoned even though she is an adult. Although an adult who committed adultery is put to death by strangulation (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 3:4, 10).
any na'arah who has no fine. See above 1:9-10.
her conception was not in holiness and her birth was in holiness. That her mother conceived while still a gentile and gave birth to her after converting.
his yevamah whom he married. That he married the wife of his brother who died childless.
that he had relations with her. The husband.
and brings out a bad name in the normal manner. That he claims she committed adultery in ordinary intercourse.
rebellion lashes. Lashes by rabbinic law.
for the witnesses are put to death if they are proven conspiring. For if they had not been refuted, the woman would be put to death for committing adultery while betrothed.
a respectful expression, that they negotiate over the hidden matters. A euphemism, meaning the investigation and exposure of private matters, and not dealing with the findings regarding virginity.
that she is exempt from everything. For the absence of virginity is not grounds for punishment (as above halakhah 6).
and the one who had relations with her is liable for monetary payments only. As detailed in the first two chapters.
